summary: Dor reinterprets the equality of Godement–Jacquet and Jacquet–Langlands L-functions for GL(2) as structure. Over a non-archimedean local field F, the Weil representation of the metaplectic cover of Sp(M_2(F) ⊗ W) gives Y = S(M_2(F) × F^×) a third, hidden GL_2(F)-action, part of a triality S_3 ⋉ GL_2(F)³ (Proposition 2.12). Ṽ ⊗_G Y ⊗_G V is then the Kirillov model of V for generic V, compatibly with zeta integrals (Theorem 2.2, Proposition 2.5). Reading Y as a bifunctor V ⊛ V' = V ⊗_G Y ⊗_G V' gives a unital weak symmetric monoidal structure on Mod(GL_2(F)) with unit the Whittaker space. It is the tensor product over the Bernstein centre on degeneracy-free representations (Theorem 3.26) and on spherical ones (Theorem 3.42), and extends uniquely to a symmetric monoidal structure (Theorem 3.52), in which generic irreducibles are idempotent algebras. Over a global function field, a theta functional makes the automorphic functions orthogonal to characters a commutative ⊛-algebra ℐ, whose unit, given by Poincaré series, is surjective (Proposition 4.19, Corollary 4.22). ℐ-modules form a full subcategory, the abstractly automorphic representations, which contains all automorphic representations and is closed under subquotients and contragredients. A spin structure yields a convolution algebra of spherical automorphic functions (Appendix A). The ingredients are planned in the atlas (MetaplecticAutomorphicForms, AL.2, SR.3, SR.5, R16.2/R16.5, and Mathlib's categorical notions), but the structure itself goes in no existing direction and is routed to a new roadmap. One misprint is recorded.

items.name: Symmetric monoidal categories, commutative algebra objects and their module categories
items.statement: A symmetric monoidal category (C, ⊗, 1_C) with associator, unitors and symmetry; a commutative unital algebra object A ∈ C (multiplication A ⊗ A → A and unit 1_C → A satisfying associativity, commutativity and unitality); and the category of A-modules in C, objects M with action A ⊗ M → M satisfying the usual axioms.
items.note: Read at the pinned Mathlib: SymmetricCategory (Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Monoidal/Braided/Basic.lean:367), CommMon (Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Monoidal/CommMon_.lean:27, commutative monoid objects), ModObj (Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Monoidal/Mod.lean:59, module objects over a monoid object). The paper also uses the Lurie tensor product of C-linear presentable categories (Remark 3.54), which is not in the libraries.

items.name: Godement–Jacquet zeta integrals for GL(2)
items.statement: Locally, for a matrix coefficient β of V and Ψ ∈ S(M_2(F)), Z_GJ(β, Ψ, s) = ∫_{GL_2(F)} β(g)Ψ(g)|det g|^{s+1/2} d^×g; globally, for an automorphic representation V, Ψ ∈ S(M_2(A)) and β ∈ V ⊗ Ṽ, the adelic integral (1.1); and for φ, φ' ∈ S, Z_GJ(φ', φ, Ψ, s) = ∫_{GL_2(A)} (∫_{GL_2(F)\GL_2(A)} φ'(h^{−T})φ(hg) d^×h) Ψ(g)|det g|^{s+1/2} d^×g. The Godement–Jacquet L-function is the gcd of these integrals.
items.note: AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors AL.2 plans Godement–Jacquet local zeta integrals from Schwartz functions on M_n and matrix coefficients, and the adelic global integral.

items.name: Kirillov and Whittaker models of generic representations of GL(2) via the Bernstein–Zelevinsky functors Φ^±
items.statement: Let F be a non-archimedean local field with char(F) ≠ 2, G = GL_2(F) with the Haar measure giving a maximal compact subgroup volume 1, e: F → C^× a nontrivial additive character and θ(1 u; 0 1) = e(u) on U = U_2(F). Let P be the mirabolic subgroup, Φ^−: Mod(P) → Vect the θ-equivariant quotient and Φ^+ its left adjoint (θ-equivariant compact induction; Bernstein–Zelevinsky 1977, Proposition 3.2). For generic irreducible V, Φ^−Ṽ is one-dimensional; a vector in it gives S(F^×) ≅ Φ^+C → Ṽ and dually an injective map of P-modules V → S(F^×) (P acting by (a b; 0 1)·f(y) = e(by)f(ay)), unique up to scalar, whose image is the Kirillov model K(V), with its canonical G-action. The Whittaker space 1 is the compact induction of S(F^×) from P to G, and the Whittaker model is the image of the dual map V → 1̃. V(n) denotes the twist by |det|^n.
items.note: SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups SR.5 plans Bernstein–Zelevinsky derivatives and Whittaker functionals for GL_n, and GL2AutomorphicRepresentationsAndTransfer R16.2 their specialisation to GL_2.

items.name: Jacquet–Langlands (Hecke) zeta integrals for GL(2)
items.statement: Globally, for an automorphic form φ with Whittaker function W_φ, Z_JL(φ, s) = ∫_{A^×/F^×} φ((y 0; 0 1))|y|^{s−1/2} d^×y (1.2), equivalently ∫_{A^×} W_φ((y 0; 0 1))|y|^{s−1/2} d^×y; locally, for w in a Kirillov model, Z_JL(w, s) = ∫_{F^×} w(y)|y|^{s−1/2} d^×y.
items.locator: (1.2) and Remark 1.1, p. 4; Proposition 2.5, p. 10; §4.1, p. 39
items.note: GL2AutomorphicRepresentationsAndTransfer R16.5 plans 'the GL₂ global Whittaker expansion and its identification with those integral models'.

items.name: The Heisenberg group, the metaplectic group Mp(V), the Weil representation and its Schrödinger model
items.statement: For a symplectic space V over F, H(V) = V × F with (v, x)(v', x') = (v + v', ½⟨v, v'⟩ + x + x'); it has a unique irreducible representation (π, X) with central character e. Mp(V) is the group of pairs (g, γ) with g ∈ Sp(V) and γ: π ≅ π^g, an extension 1 → C^× → Mp(V) → Sp(V) → 1 acting on X (the Weil representation). For a Lagrangian L with a splitting p: V → L, X = S(L) with π(v, x)Ψ(ℓ) = e(−⟨v, ℓ + ½p(v)⟩ + x)Ψ(ℓ + p(v)) (the Schrödinger model).
items.note: MetaplecticAutomorphicForms MP.0–MP.2 plan the Heisenberg group, Schrödinger models, Stone–von Neumann, the metaplectic extension and explicit operator formulas.

items.name: Theta functionals are invariant under rational points, by adelic Poisson summation (function-field case)
items.statement: For a global function field F of characteristic ≠ 2 and a Schwartz function Φ on the adelic points of a rational symplectic datum, the theta functional Φ ↦ Σ_{ξ ∈ M_2(F)} Φ(ξ) on S(M_2(A)) is invariant under the rational points of the metaplectic group used to construct Y_A; in particular Poisson summation Σ_ξ Ψ(ξ, q) = Σ_ξ ∫_{M_2(A)} Ψ(h, q) e(−tr(ξ^T h)) dh holds.
items.note: AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors AL.0 ('adelic Poisson summation, with the diagonal lattice and volume from GlobalNumberFields') and MetaplecticAutomorphicForms MP.4–MP.5 (the rational splitting and theta series) plan this over number fields; the paper works over function fields, which those layers do not state.

items.name: The G-bimodule Y = S(M_2(F) × F^×), its open part Y° and the isomorphism μ
items.statement: Let F be a non-archimedean local field with char(F) ≠ 2, G = GL_2(F) with the Haar measure giving a maximal compact subgroup volume 1, e: F → C^× a nontrivial additive character and θ(1 u; 0 1) = e(u) on U = U_2(F). Y = S(M_2(F) × F^×) with h·(g, y)·h' = (hgh', y·det(hh')^{−1}) (2.1), a G-bimodule; Ṽ ⊗_G S(M_2(F)) ⊗_G V is the space of F^×-coinvariants of Ṽ ⊗_G Y ⊗_G V. For Y° = S(GL_2(F) × F^×) ⊂ Y there is a canonical isomorphism μ: Ṽ ⊗_G Y° ⊗_G V ≅ S(F^×), ṽ ⊗ Ψ ⊗ v ↦ ∫_{GL_2(F)} ⟨ṽ, π(g)v⟩ Ψ(g, y det(g)^{−1}) d^×g (2.2).

items.name: Constructions 2.7 and 2.9: the symplectic space M_2(F) ⊗ W and the action of S_3 ⋉ G^{3,det=1}
items.statement: With U = M_2(F), W a two-dimensional symplectic space and ⟨m, m'⟩ = tr(m)tr(m') − tr(mm') the polarisation of det, U ⊗ W is symplectic via ⟨m ⊗ v, m' ⊗ v'⟩ = (v ∧ v')⟨m, m'⟩. G^{3,det=1} = {(g_1, g_2, g_3) ∈ G³ : det(g_1g_2g_3) = 1} acts by (g_1, g_2, g_3)(m ⊗ v) = g_1 m g_3^T ⊗ g_2 v, extending to S_3 ⋉ G^{3,det=1} → Sp(U ⊗ W) with (1, 3)(m ⊗ v) = m^T ⊗ v (the three factors act symmetrically, U ⊗ W ≅ W ⊗ W^∨ ⊗ W).
items.locator: Construction 2.7, p. 11; Remark 2.8, p. 11; Construction 2.9, p. 11

items.name: Proposition 2.12: the unique metaplectic lift of S_3 ⋉ G^{3,det=1}
items.statement: Consider the Schrödinger model of the Weil representation of Mp(U ⊗ W) on S(M_2(F)) for the Lagrangian M_2(F) ⊗ e_2 and the splitting with kernel M_2(F) ⊗ e_1 (Construction 2.11). There is a unique lift S_3 ⋉ G^{3,det=1} → Mp(U ⊗ W) of Construction 2.9 such that (1, 3) acts on S(M_2(F)) by the transposition g ↦ g^T. Explicitly (g_1, 1, g_3)Ψ(m) = Ψ(g_1^{−1} m g_3^{−T}) on SL_2(F) × 1 × SL_2(F), the middle SL_2(F) acts by (2.6)–(2.8) (e(b det m)Ψ(m), |t|²Ψ(tm), and a Fourier transform on M_2(F)), the torus (F^×)^{3,Π=1} by (2.9), and an order-3 permutation σ by (2.11).
items.locator: Proposition 2.12, p. 12; Construction 2.11, p. 12; proof pp. 13–14
items.note: Uniqueness: the abelianisation of S_3 ⋉ G^{3,det=1} is Z/2, generated by (1, 3). Existence: each SL_2(F) factor lifts uniquely, then S_2 ⋉ (F^×)^{3,Π=1} and σ with τστ^{−1} = σ². Corrected for source issue E1.

items.name: Construction 2.13: the middle action of G on Y
items.statement: Identify Y = S(M_2(F) × F^×) = cInd_{S_3⋉G^{3,det=1}}^{S_3⋉G^3} S(M_2(F)) via the section y ↦ (1, diag(y, 1), 1) with a determinant twist: for Ψ(m, y) = Φ(m)f(y), ((g_1, g_2, g_3)·Ψ)(m, y) = |det(g_1g_2g_3)|·((g_1, diag(y,1)^{−1} g_2 diag(y det(g_1g_2g_3)^{−1}, 1), g_3)·Φ)(m) f(y det(g_1g_2g_3)) (2.4). This extends Proposition 2.12 to an action of S_3 ⋉ G³ on Y; the middle copy of G is the middle action. (g_1, 1, g_3)Ψ(g, y) = Ψ(g_1^{−1} g g_3^{−T}, y det(g_1g_3^T)) and (1, 3)Ψ(g, y) = Ψ(g^T, y).
items.locator: Construction 2.13, p. 12; Example 2.14, p. 12; Example 2.15, p. 13; Remark 2.16, p. 13

items.name: Theorem 2.2: the hidden third action of G on Y and the spectral decomposition of Y at generic representations
items.statement: Let F be a non-archimedean local field with char(F) ≠ 2, G = GL_2(F) with the Haar measure giving a maximal compact subgroup volume 1, e: F → C^× a nontrivial additive character and θ(1 u; 0 1) = e(u) on U = U_2(F). There is a canonical G-action τ on Y (the middle action), uniquely determined by: (1) τ commutes with the left and right G-actions; (2) for every generic irreducible (π, V) there is an isomorphism of G-modules ν: Ṽ ⊗_G Y ⊗_G V ≅ K(V(−1))(1); (3) ν restricts on Ṽ ⊗_G Y° ⊗_G V to μ: → S(F^×) followed by the inclusion S(F^×) ⊂ K(V(−1))(1) of the Kirillov model. In particular Ṽ ⊗_G S(M_2(F)) ⊗_G V ≅ K(V(−1))(1)/F^×, one-dimensional.
items.locator: Theorem 2.2, p. 9; Remarks 2.3–2.4, p. 9; proof in §2.3, pp. 14–17
items.note: The inclusion S(F^×) ⊂ K(V(−1))(1) is |det|-twisted P-equivariant, reflecting the shift s ± 1/2 between the two zeta integrals (Remark 2.4).

items.name: Proposition 2.5: ν intertwines Godement–Jacquet and Jacquet–Langlands zeta integrals
items.statement: For Ψ ⊗ f ∈ S(M_2(F)) ⊗ S(F^×) = Y, a matrix coefficient β of V and the canonical j: K(V(−1))(1) ≅ K(V), Z_JL(j ∘ ν(β ⊗ Ψ ⊗ f), s) = Z_GJ(β, Ψ, s) · ∫_{F^×} f(y)|y|^{s+1/2} d^×y. Hence the two constructions give the same L-function.

items.name: Lemma 2.17: the three Bernstein-centre actions on Y coincide
items.statement: Viewing Y as a G³-module through the left, middle and right actions, the three resulting actions of the Bernstein centre of G on Y coincide (the centre is fixed by g ↦ g^T, Remark 2.18).
items.note: The Bernstein centre itself is planned in SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups SR.3.

items.name: Lemma 2.19: Φ^+Φ^−Y = Y° for the middle action
items.statement: With Φ^± taken for the middle action, the natural map Φ^+Φ^−Y → Y is injective with image Y° (functions supported away from {det(g)y = 0}); the middle action of (a b; 0 1) is (a b; 0 1)·Ψ(g, y) = |a|·e(b det(g) y)·Ψ(g, ay) (2.12).

items.name: Lemma 2.20: the degenerate part of Y and Jacquet modules
items.statement: Let (π, V) be a representation of G such that V and Ṽ admit no SL_2(F)-invariant linear functionals, and Jac the Jacquet functor to the diagonal torus F^× × F^×. Then Ṽ ⊗_G S(M_2^{det=0}(F) × F^×) ⊗_G V ≅ Jac(Ṽ) ⊗_{F^××F^×} Jac(V).
items.note: Uses 0 → S(P\G) ⊗_{F^×} S(P\G) → S(M_2^{det=0}(F)) → 1_G → 0 and the Tor spectral sequence to kill Tor_1.

items.name: Remarks 2.21–2.24: explicit formulas for ν and the middle action
items.statement: ν(ṽ ⊗ Ψ ⊗ v)(y) = ∫_{GL_2(F)} ⟨ṽ, π(g)v⟩ Ψ(g, det(g)^{−1}y) d^×g; Y° generates Y under the middle action; informally Y ≅ ∫ V ⊗ K(V(−1))(1) ⊗ Ṽ; and the middle action of w = (0 −1; 1 0) is w·Ψ(g, y) = |y|² ∫_{M_2(F)} Ψ(h, y) e(−y⟨g, h⟩) dh, for the self-dual measure on M_2(F).

items.name: Definition 3.2 and Construction 3.3: left and right modules via transposition, and the bifunctor ⊛
items.statement: Mod(G) is the category of smooth left G-modules over C; I_RL: Mod_L(G) → Mod_R(G) sends (π_L, M) to π_R(g) = π_L(g^T) (not g^{−1}), so that the centre acts compatibly, with inverse I_LR. The bifunctor ⊛: Mod(G) × Mod(G) → Mod(G) is V ⊛ V' = (I_RL(V) ⊗ I_RL(V')) ⊗_{G×G} Y, using the left and right translation actions on Y, with G acting through the middle action. The transposition of M_2(F) gives a symmetry V ⊛ V' ≅ V' ⊛ V (Remark 3.4); by Proposition 2.12 the choice of which two actions to contract is immaterial (Remark 3.5); ⊛ preserves colimits (Remark 3.6).
items.locator: Definition 3.2, p. 19; Construction 3.3, p. 19; Remarks 3.4–3.6, p. 20; Remark 3.1

items.name: Definitions 3.7–3.8: weak symmetric monoidal categories and functors
items.statement: A weak symmetric monoidal structure on a category C is a bifunctor ⊗ with an object 1_C and natural isomorphisms s_{A,B}: A ⊗ B ≅ B ⊗ A and l_A: 1_C ⊗ A ≅ A with s_{B,A} ∘ s_{A,B} = id and l_{1_C} ∘ s_{1_C,1_C} = l_{1_C} (no associativity data); a weak symmetric monoidal functor carries isomorphisms 1_D ≅ F(1_C), F(A) ⊗ F(B) ≅ F(A ⊗ B) compatible with s and l. Equivalently, algebras in categories over the operad O_w of binary trees with unordered children (Remark 3.9).
items.locator: Definition 3.7, p. 20; Definition 3.8, p. 21; Remark 3.9, p. 21
items.note: Mathlib has monoidal, braided and symmetric categories (item 001) but not this associativity-free notion.

items.name: Construction 3.10 and Construction 3.16: the unit 1 (the Whittaker space) and the unit isomorphism 1 ⊛ M ≅ M
items.statement: 1 is the space of θ-coinvariants of S(G) for the right action (Φ^− applied to S(G)), with left action (π(h)f)(g) = f(gh); a Haar measure on U identifies it with cInd_U^G(θ) (Remark 3.15). There is a canonical natural isomorphism 1 ⊛ M ≅ M, built from the isomorphism φ: I_RL(1) ⊗_G Y ≅ S(G) (middle action), f ⊗ Ψ ↦ ∫_G f(h)·(wh^{−T}·Ψ)(g^{−1}, −det g) d^×h (3.3); and Φ^−(M ⊛ N) ≅ I_RL(M) ⊗_G N (Remark 3.17).
items.locator: Construction 3.10, p. 22; Construction 3.16, p. 22; Remarks 3.11–3.17, pp. 22–23; (3.3)

items.name: Claim 3.18: the braiding of 1 ⊛ 1 is trivial
items.statement: The automorphism λ: 1 → 1 of (3.4), obtained from the unit isomorphism and the symmetry of ⊛, is the identity.
items.note: Proof by the Gelfand–Kazhdan technique: decompose M_2(F) × F^× into U × U-orbits and show that the orbits carrying θ-equivariant distributions are transposition-invariant (Bernstein–Zelevinsky 1976, Theorem 6.10).

items.name: Corollaries 3.20–3.21: End(1) is commutative, and (⊛, 1) is a weak symmetric monoidal structure on Mod(G)
items.statement: The ring End(1) is commutative (an Eckmann–Hilton argument using only Claim 3.18), and ⊛ with the unit 1, the isomorphism of Construction 3.16 and the symmetry of Remark 3.4 is a weak symmetric monoidal structure on Mod(G).

items.name: Definitions 3.22–3.23: degenerate and degeneracy-free representations
items.statement: M ∈ Mod(G) is degenerate if Φ^−(M) = 0; N is degeneracy-free if Ext^i(N, M) = 0 for all degenerate M and i = 0, 1; Mod^{deg-free}(G) is the full subcategory. Equivalently it is the smallest full subcategory containing 1 and closed under colimits, and it is equivalent (via the left adjoint of the quotient functor) to the quotient of Mod(G) by degenerate representations. Most generic irreducibles are degeneracy-free, but the Steinberg representation St is not, while the non-trivial extension 1_G^St of St and 1_G is (Warning 3.25).
items.locator: Definition 3.22, p. 25; Definition 3.23, p. 25; Remark 3.24; Warning 3.25

items.name: The quasi-unital ring Z = ⊕_c Z_c of Bernstein centres and its smooth modules
items.statement: Z = ⊕_c Z_c, the direct sum of the Bernstein centres of the Bernstein components c of Mod(G), is quasi-unital (Z ⊗_Z Z ≅ Z); Mod(Z) is the symmetric monoidal category of smooth Z-modules (Z ⊗_Z M ≅ M) with the relative tensor product ⊗_Z, and it acts on Mod(G). Φ^− factors through Φ^−_enh: Mod(G) → Mod(Z), and Hom(M, N) ⊆ Hom(M, N) denotes morphisms supported on finitely many components, Hom(M, N) = Z ⊗_{Z(Mod(G))} Hom(M, N).
items.note: Quasi-unital rings and their smooth modules are from Dor, The Dixmier–Malliavin theorem and bornological vector spaces (arXiv:2001.05694), §3; the Bernstein centre is planned in SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups SR.3.

items.name: Claims 3.30, 3.32, 3.33 and Lemma 3.35: the adjunction for 1, End(1) = Z, and generation of degeneracy-free representations
items.statement: Claim 3.30: − ⊗_Z 1: Mod(Z) → Mod(G) is left adjoint to Φ^−_enh (equivalently Φ^−_enh M ≅ Hom(1, M); the adjunction depends on the Haar measure on U). Lemma 3.35: for M in a single Bernstein component, M → S(P) ⊗_{S(P)} Hom_G(S(G), M) becomes an isomorphism after Φ^−. Claim 3.32: Z → Hom(1, 1) is an isomorphism. Claim 3.33: the smallest full subcategory of Mod(G) containing 1 and closed under colimits is Mod^{deg-free}(G).
items.locator: Claim 3.30, p. 27; Claim 3.32, p. 27; Claim 3.33, p. 27; Lemma 3.35, p. 29; Remark 3.29

items.name: Theorem 3.26 and Corollary 3.27: ⊛ on degeneracy-free representations is the tensor product over the centre
items.statement: The functor − ⊗_Z 1: Mod(Z) → Mod(G) is fully faithful with essential image Mod^{deg-free}(G), and it is weak symmetric monoidal (so ⊛ restricted to Mod^{deg-free}(G) is ⊗_Z). Consequently ⊛ on Mod^{deg-free}(G) extends to a symmetric monoidal structure, uniquely up to unique isomorphism. (⊛ does not descend to the quotient by degenerate representations: 1_G ⊛ 1_G = 1_G^St, Remark 3.28.)

items.name: Definition 3.36: the spherical generator E = cInd_K^G S(O^×) and spherical representations
items.statement: With K = GL_2(O), E = cInd_K^G(S(O^×)) (K acting on S(O^×) through det) ≅ cInd_{SL_2(O)}^G 1; Mod^sph(G) is the smallest full subcategory containing E closed under colimits. Hom(E, M) ≅ Hom(S(G), M)^{SL_2(O)} (Remark 3.39); E lives on the Bernstein components containing a one-dimensional representation, whose centres form the quasi-unital Z_sph.

items.name: Constructions 3.44–3.45: the counit ε: E → 1 and the comultiplication μ: E → E ⊛ E
items.statement: Let ν(e) be the largest integer with e(ϖ^{−ν(e)}O) = 1. ε is defined by the SL_2(O)-invariant, right θ-equivariant distribution f(g) = e(b)δ_1(det k) on g = (1 b; 0 1)(0 1; −ϖ^{ν(e)} 0)k (0 elsewhere); μ by the S_3 ⋉ SL_2(O)³-invariant distribution q^{−ν(e)}·1_{M_2(O)}(g)δ_{ϖ^{−ν(e)}}(y) on M_2(F) × F^× (for ν(e) = 0, the distinguished Godement–Jacquet test function 1_{M_2(O)} times δ_1). μ is symmetric (Remark 3.48); the choices amount to an unramified spin structure (Remark 3.47).
items.locator: Construction 3.44, p. 31; Construction 3.45, p. 32; Remarks 3.46–3.48, pp. 32–33

items.name: Claim 3.49 and Theorem 3.42: E is idempotent, and ⊛ on spherical representations is ⊗_{Z_sph}
items.statement: The diagram E → E ⊛ E → E ⊛ 1 ≅ E (via μ and id ⊛ ε) is the identity, and μ: E → E ⊛ E is an isomorphism. Hence − ⊗_{Z_sph} E: Mod(Z_sph) → Mod(G) is fully faithful with essential image Mod^sph(G), sending Z_sph and ⊗_{Z_sph} to E and ⊛ (it is not weak symmetric monoidal, since it does not respect the unit).

items.name: Corollary 3.51: the weak symmetric monoidal functor from Mod(Z) × Mod(Z_sph)
items.statement: Give Mod(Z) × Mod(Z_sph) the colimit-preserving Z-linear symmetric monoidal structure with unit (Z, 0) and (0, Z_sph) idempotent, (M_0, N_0) ⊗ (M_1, N_1) = (M_0 ⊗_Z M_1, M_0 ⊗_Z N_1 ⊕ N_0 ⊗_Z M_1 ⊕ N_0 ⊗_Z N_1). Then (M, N) ↦ (M ⊗_Z 1) ⊕ (N ⊗_{Z_sph} E) is a faithful weak symmetric monoidal functor to Mod(G).

items.name: The idempotent theorem of Gurevich–Hadani
items.statement: For an idempotent object E (with an isomorphism E ≅ E ⊗ E compatible with a counit), any associator on E ⊗ E ⊗ E compatible with the pentagon axiom is forced, a map a: E → E satisfying a² = a³ being the identity; consequently an idempotent counital coalgebra is coassociative (Gurevich–Hadani, The categorical Weil representation, Theorem 3.1.2).
items.locator: Proof of Claim 3.58, pp. 36–37; Remark 3.56; Claim A.6

items.name: Claim 3.58 and Theorem 3.52: ⊛ extends uniquely to a symmetric monoidal structure on Mod(G)
items.statement: Let F be a non-archimedean local field with char(F) ≠ 2, G = GL_2(F) with the Haar measure giving a maximal compact subgroup volume 1, e: F → C^× a nontrivial additive character and θ(1 u; 0 1) = e(u) on U = U_2(F). There is a unique extension of the weak symmetric monoidal structure (⊛, 1) to a symmetric monoidal structure on Mod(G); for it, the functor Mod(Z) × Mod(Z_sph) → Mod(G) of Corollary 3.51 is symmetric monoidal. The extension does not depend on the (non-canonical) choice of isomorphism E ≅ E ⊛ E.
items.locator: Theorem 3.52, p. 35; Claim 3.58, p. 36; Remark 3.53; proof pp. 37–38
items.note: Mod(G) is generated as a Z-linear category by 1 and E, so ⊛ is the left Kan extension of its restriction to finite sums of 1 and E; the associators from Mod(Z) × Mod(Z_sph) are checked to be natural for maps between 1 and E.

items.name: Remark 3.54: Mod(G) with ⊛ is a commutative Frobenius algebra in C-linear presentable categories
items.statement: Φ^−: Mod(G) → Vect is a trace: Φ^− ∘ ⊛ is the pairing M ⊠ N ↦ I_RL(M) ⊗_G N, a perfect pairing exhibiting Mod(G) as self-dual in the symmetric monoidal 2-category of C-linear presentable categories with the Lurie tensor product.

items.name: Example 3.55: generic irreducible representations are idempotent commutative algebras for ⊛
items.statement: For V ∈ Mod(G) there is a canonical map 1 ⊗ Hom_G(1, V) → V ⊛ V; for V generic irreducible it is an isomorphism, so V ⊛ V ≅ V after a choice of Whittaker functional (the reformulation of Theorem 2.2). Moreover, a nonzero v_gen ∈ Φ^−V = Hom_G(1, V) makes V a unital commutative ⊛-algebra, by the general fact that in a symmetric monoidal abelian category with right exact tensor product a surjection 1 ↠ X gives X ≅ X ⊗ X and a commutative unital algebra structure on X.

items.name: Remarks 3.56–3.57: E is a cocommutative coalgebra, and coinvariants of ⊛-algebras become ⊗-algebras
items.statement: E is a counital cocommutative coassociative coalgebra for ⊛. Hence, for a unital commutative ⊛-algebra V, V/SL_2(O) = Hom(E, V) is a quasi-unital commutative Z_sph-algebra and Φ^−V = Hom(1, V) a quasi-unital commutative Z-algebra for the usual tensor product, compatibly with Z → Z_sph.

items.name: The global space Y_A, the global product ⊛ and the global unit 1 (§4.2, Claim 4.3, Corollary 4.4)
items.statement: Let F be a global function field of characteristic ≠ 2, A its adeles, G = GL_2(A) with the Haar measures giving the maximal compact subgroups volume 1, and e: A/F → C^× a fixed nontrivial additive character. Y_A = S(M_2(A) × A^×) is the restricted tensor product of the Y_v with respect to y_v = 1_{M_2(O_v)}(g)1_{O_v^×}(y), with the GL_2(A)³-action of Construction 2.13; V ⊛ V' = V ⊗_G Y_A ⊗_G V'; the global unit 1 is the θ-coinvariants of S(GL_2(A)) for the right action of U(A), θ(1 u; 0 1) = e(u), ≅ cInd_{U(A)}^G(θ) (Remark 4.2). For almost all v, the unit isomorphism, the transposition and the associativity constraint fix the distinguished vectors (Claim 4.3), so the local data define a symmetric monoidal structure ⊛ on Mod(GL_2(A)) (Corollary 4.4).

items.name: The space S of automorphic functions and its subspace ℐ orthogonal to characters
items.statement: Let F be a global function field of characteristic ≠ 2, A its adeles, G = GL_2(A) with the Haar measures giving the maximal compact subgroups volume 1, and e: A/F → C^× a fixed nontrivial additive character. S = S(GL_2(F)\GL_2(A)) is the space of smooth compactly supported functions on the automorphic quotient, p: S → S(A^×/F^×) the projection along det, and ℐ = ker p, the functions orthogonal to all χ(det g); S̃ (the smoothening of the dual) is the space of smooth functions on GL_2(F)\GL_2(A) with no growth condition.

items.name: Definition 4.5: the theta functional μ on Y_A
items.statement: μ: Y_A → C, μ(Ψ) = Σ_{(ξ, q) ∈ M_2(F) × F^×} Ψ(ξ, q). It is invariant under the left and right actions of GL_2(F), under the middle action of the mirabolic P_2(F) (by (2.12)), and under transposition of M_2(A).

items.name: Proposition 4.9: μ is invariant under S_3 ⋉ GL_2(F)³
items.statement: The functional μ: Y_A → C is invariant under the S_3 ⋉ GL_2(F)³-action of Remark 3.5; in particular under the middle action of GL_2(F).
items.note: By Remark 4.6 it suffices to treat w = (0 −1; 1 0); with ⟨ξ, h⟩ = tr(w^{−1}ξ^T w h) and |q| = 1 for q ∈ F^×, this is Poisson summation (item 006).

items.name: Construction 4.10 and Remark 4.11: the multiplication m: S ⊛ S → S̃ and its compatibility with zeta integrals
items.statement: m is the composite S ⊛ S ≅ GL_2(F)\Y_A/GL_2(F) → S̃, Ψ ↦ (g ↦ μ(g·Ψ)) (middle action), a kind of theta lift. It sends Godement–Jacquet to Jacquet–Langlands zeta integrals: Z_JL(m(φ' ⊗ Ψ ⊗ f ⊗ φ), s) = Z_GJ(φ', φ, Ψ, s)·∫_{A^×} f(y)|y|^{s+1/2} d^×y for Ψ ⊗ f ∈ Y_A and φ, φ' ∈ S (Whittaker functions taken with U(A)/U(F) of volume 1).

items.name: Constructions 4.13 and 4.15, Claim 4.14: the Whittaker coefficient W and the unit e: 1 → S by Poincaré series
items.statement: W: S̃ → 1̃ sends φ to its Whittaker function W_φ(g) = ∫_{U(A)/U(F)} φ(ug)θ(u) du (total volume 1). There is a unique map e: 1 → S whose contragredient is W; it sends W ∈ cInd_{U(A)}^G(θ) ≅ 1 to the Poincaré series Σ_{γ ∈ U_2(F)\GL_2(F)} W(γg) ∈ S.
items.locator: Construction 4.13, p. 45; Claim 4.14, p. 45; Construction 4.15, p. 45

items.name: Proposition 4.16 and Corollary 4.18: unitality of m, through the Petersson pairing
items.statement: The composite S ⊗_G S ≅ 1 ⊗_G (S ⊛ S) → S ⊗_G (S ⊛ S) → C (via e ⊗ id and μ) is the Petersson pairing ρ(f ⊗ f') = ∫_{GL_2(A)} f(g)f'(g^{−T}) d^×g (independently of the slot, by Proposition 4.9). Hence S ≅ 1 ⊛ S → S ⊛ S → S̃ (via e and m) is the inclusion S ⊆ S̃.

items.name: Proposition 4.19: the image of the unit e: 1 → S is ℐ
items.statement: The image of e: 1 → S is ℐ: dually, a smooth function φ on GL_2(F)\GL_2(A) with W_φ = 0 is invariant under the subgroup generated by U(A) and GL_2(F), which contains SL_2(A), so it factors through det.
items.note: Remark 4.20 compares this with multiplicity one.

items.name: Corollaries 4.21–4.22 and Remarks 4.23–4.24: ℐ is a unital commutative ⊛-algebra with an invariant pairing
items.statement: m(ℐ ⊛ ℐ) ⊆ ℐ, and m makes ℐ a unital commutative algebra in (Mod(GL_2(A)), ⊛) with unit e; since e is surjective, m is the unique multiplication with this unit. The Petersson pairing induces ⟨−, −⟩: ℐ ⊗_G ℐ = Φ^−(ℐ ⊛ ℐ) → C with ⟨x, yz⟩ = ⟨xy, z⟩; ℐ is not a Frobenius algebra (ℐ → ℐ̃ is not an isomorphism).

items.name: Corollaries 4.25–4.26 and Remark 4.27: S is an ℐ-module, with a symmetric triality
items.statement: m(ℐ ⊛ S) ⊆ S, and m makes S an ℐ-module for ⊛. The map m: S ⊛ S → S̃ defines a symmetric triality Φ^−(S ⊛ S ⊛ S) → C which respects the ℐ-module structure.

items.name: Claim 4.28, Definition 4.29 and Remark 4.30: abstractly automorphic representations
items.statement: The forgetful functor Mod(ℐ) → Mod(GL_2(A)) from ℐ-modules in (Mod(GL_2(A)), ⊛) is fully faithful (by Proposition 4.19). V ∈ Mod(GL_2(A)) is abstractly automorphic if it lies in its essential image Mod^aut(GL_2(A)); equivalently the canonical map 1 ⊛ V → V factors through ℐ ⊛ V.

items.name: Proposition 4.32 and Remark 4.33: closure properties; automorphic representations are abstractly automorphic
items.statement: Mod^aut(GL_2(A)) is closed under subquotients and contragredients in Mod(GL_2(A)). Since S is abstractly automorphic, so is S̃, and every irreducible automorphic representation (a subquotient of it) is abstractly automorphic.

items.name: Example 4.35: the Godement–Jacquet test-function space is abstractly automorphic
items.statement: ℒ = S(M_2(A))_{GL_2(F)}, the GL_2(F)-coinvariants for one of the two actions, equals S ⊛ S(A\G) with A = diag(A^×, 1) ≅ G_m, and is abstractly automorphic.

items.name: Results announced from the sequel: irreducible abstractly automorphic representations and the Eisenstein–cuspidal decomposition
items.statement: The irreducible objects of Mod^aut(GL_2(A)) are exactly the irreducible automorphic representations (subquotients of S̃), and Mod^aut(GL_2(A)) decomposes into components induced from GL(1) × GL(1) (Eisenstein) and cuspidal components, with constant terms and Eisenstein series as adjoint functors.
items.locator: §1.2, p. 5 (proofs in Dor, Global parabolic induction and abstract automorphicity, arXiv:2102.11820)
items.note: Stated, not proved, in this paper; recorded so the new roadmap plans them with their actual source.

items.name: Definition A.1 and Remark A.2: unramified spin structures on the curve of F
items.statement: Let C be the smooth proper curve with function field F and Ω its canonical bundle. An unramified spin structure is a line bundle L on C with an isomorphism η: L ⊗ L ≅ Ω; one always exists (Armitage 1967).

items.name: Definition A.4, Construction A.5 and Claim A.6: the global spherical coalgebra E_A
items.statement: Fix (L, η) and a rational section s with e corresponding to η(s ⊗ s) via the sum of residues; e has even valuation at every place, so there is a unique self-dual O_A-lattice Λ ⊂ A. E_A = cInd_{SL_2(O_A)}^G(1), with comultiplication μ: E_A → E_A ⊛ E_A induced by the S_3 ⋉ SL_2(O_A)³-invariant distribution 1_{M_2(Λ)}(g)δ_1(y); E_A is a counital cocommutative coassociative coalgebra.
items.locator: Definition A.4, p. 51; Construction A.5, p. 51; Claim A.6, p. 51; Remark A.3

items.name: Construction A.7 and Remark A.8: the convolution algebra of spherical automorphic functions
items.statement: ℐ_{SL_2(O_A)} = Hom(E_A, ℐ) acquires a canonical quasi-unital commutative algebra structure over the centre of Mod(G) for the usual tensor product, independent of the section s; it is invariant under ι(f)(g) = |det g|^{−2} f(g^{−T}). This is the 'spectral Fourier transform' of §1.3: it identifies spherical automorphic functions with functions on the unramified automorphic spectrum.
items.locator: Construction A.7, p. 51; Remark A.8; §1.3, p. 6
